messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER/ALERT — High p95 latency observed for hosted generation API in eu-west-1. Severity: high. Affected endpoint: /v1/generate (streaming + sync). Trigger: sustained p95 > 1s for 3+ minutes. Pager: https://pd.redwood.example/incident/INC-1769123456
Leah (oncall): ack — I'm on it. Pulling dashboards and logs now.
Leah (oncall): quick read — p95 jumped ~180ms -> ~1.2s starting ~1769123300. Error rate stays ~baseline, so looks like time spent in inference, not retries.
Ravi (infra): I see a canary promotion for model-quant-3 pushed to eu-west-1 at 1769123200. Canary reports didn't show this, maybe load profile differs. Do we want an immediate rollback to stable-20260301?
Maya (eng-runtime): I'm looking at runtime traces — KV cache eviction spike and multiple requests hitting fallback execution (quant->fp kernel fallback). That increases token-step latency. Hypothesis: quantized kernel selection regressed for longer contexts.
Leah (oncall): OK, two parallel mitigations: 1) route override to force fp16 variant for eu-west-1, 2) roll back model-quant-3 canary. Which is faster?
Maya (eng-runtime): route override is fastest. I can flip routing policy to prefer model-fp16-eu for production traffic for eu-west-1. That preserves capacity while rollback runs.
Dmitri (sre): I'll prepare the rollback job. Command:
```
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/model-serving model=redwood/model:stable-20260301
sleep 30
kubectl rollout status deploy/model-serving -n inference
```
I will watch readiness and drain pods after.
Leah (oncall): do route override now, Maya? I will draft status page and customer message.
Maya (eng-runtime): Doing route override: running config apply -> trafficPolicy.euwest1.preferredModel = model-fp16-eu. Patch applied. Traffic should start shifting in ~15–30s.
incident-bot: Deploy event detected: rollback job started by Dmitri. CI/CD link: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/78645
Leah (oncall): Status page draft (internal):
"We are investigating elevated latency for the Generation API in the EU (eu-west-1). Impact: increased p95 latency for some production requests; most requests are still completing, and error rates are not elevated. Mitigation: routing to an alternative model variant and rolling back the recently promoted canary. Current status: mitigation in progress; engineers are observing for recovery. Next update in 30 minutes or on significant change."
Leah (oncall): Customer-facing blurb for CS to copy:
"We're aware of increased latency impacting Generation API in our EU region. Our engineers have applied mitigations and are rolling back a recent model variant; most customers should see improved latency shortly. No elevated error rates have been observed. We'll post updates to the status page and follow up when full recovery is confirmed. If you see persistent timeouts, please share request IDs and timestamps with support."
Amelia (support): Posting to affected customers now; will add request-id request and link to status page.
Maya (eng-runtime): Rollback started by Dmitri is progressing. Watching metrics: p95 dropping from 1.2s -> 400ms already for some pods. Expect further improvement as KV cache warms.
Dmitri (sre): Rollout status: 6/6 pods updated and healthy. No crashloops.
Maya (eng-runtime): After routing + rollback metrics: p95 = ~210ms, median ~45ms. Streaming latency also improving. KV cache should warm fully in 5–10 minutes; we'll monitor tail.
Leah (oncall): Updating status page to "Mitigated — partial recovery observed; monitoring." ETA to full recovery: 10–20 minutes.
SRE Rotation: Handoff note — Leah is handing off to Ravi for monitoring window. Summary: root cause likely quantized kernel fallback under certain context lengths after canary promotion; mitigations applied: route override to fp16 variant + full rollback to stable-20260301 in eu-west-1. Current state: p95 reclaimed to ~210ms, watching for tail spikes.
Ravi (infra): Taking over monitoring. I'll keep an eye on metrics and escalate if any reappearance.
Leah (oncall): Thanks team. I'll open a follow-up postmortem ticket and add initial timeline + pointers to traces (link). Will set severity to S3 and schedule postmortem sync. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident status updated to "mitigated" by Leah. Postmortem ticket: https://pm.redwood.example/issue/INC-1769123456-postmortem
Leah (oncall): Closing active paging; keep thread for follow-up notes. If anyone sees regression, ping Ravi directly.
